subject: Business Models
title: Unbundling the Bank
description: A quick win: understand Unbundling the Bank.

hook.text: A bank bundles loans, savings, payments, insurance, and investment into one institution. Fintechs are ripping it apart.

buildup.text: Stripe handles payments. Robinhood handles investing. Venmo handles transfers. Each takes a piece of the bank.

discovery.text: Each fintech does one thing better than the bank's bundled version. Specialization beats generalization.

twist.text: Now fintechs are rebundling: Revolut offers banking, trading, insurance, and crypto in one app. The cycle continues.

climax.text: Banks have survived 600 years of disruption by eventually absorbing or acquiring the unbundlers.

punchline.text: Fintechs unbundle banks, then rebundle them. A 600-year cycle continues.

quiz.question: How are fintechs disrupting traditional banks?
options: Unbundling bank services into specialized products

details.summary: Fintech startups unbundled traditional banking into specialized products: payments, lending, investing, insurance, budgeting, and foreign exchange. Each fintech targets one banking function with a superior digital experience, collectively dismantling the universal bank model.
details.whyItMatters: Banking unbundling redistributed hundreds of billions in financial service revenue from incumbents to focused fintechs. Understanding this trend shows how regulatory and technology shifts can dismantle bundled industry structures.
takeaways: Fintechs specialize in individual banking functions with superior digital experiences
Payments, lending, investing, and insurance each became separate fintech categories
Some neobanks are now re-bundling financial services into superapp experiences

faq.question: Which fintechs unbundled which banking functions?
faq.answer: Stripe and Square took payments. LendingClub and SoFi took lending. Robinhood took investing. Lemonade took insurance. Mint and YNAB took budgeting. TransferWise took international transfers. Each built a focused product beating the bank's generalist version.

faq.question: Are banks fighting back against fintech unbundling?
faq.answer: Yes, through acquiring fintechs, launching digital-only sub-brands, improving mobile apps, partnering with fintechs via open banking APIs, and leveraging their regulatory advantages and existing customer relationships that fintechs lack.
